summary: We developed an app that tracks astronaut metrics and pops notifications when a value is considered "outside of normal" for the astronaut.  Adapted for offline environment and using statistical analysis without machine learning for a robust and easy to understand way to detect anomalies. We recomend using this app before launch, using a personal baseline and recordings of fluids and a cognitive run. During fligth, to integrate cognitive status and post fligth for tracking.
details:
ASTRA is an offline capable app, for astronauts health and mission-support platform. It combines a FastAPI onboard node with a Next.js crew console to organize medical tasks, measurements, personal baselines, laboratory results, alerts, clinical reviews, telemetry playback, and synchronization with ground control.

The project uses real Inspiration4/LOFT physiological data and NASA OSDR CBC/CMP laboratory datasets. High-frequency Parquet data is processed offline into a lightweight JSON playback, while laboratory values are evaluated against each crew member’s personal baseline. The platform uses experimental robust-statistics rules, including rolling medians, IQR-based z-scores, median/MAD baselines, hysteresis, and backend-persisted alerts.

ASTRA is designed to help astronauts and medical officers identify meaningful deviations early, maintain health tasks during communication loss, and preserve a complete audit trail for later synchronization with Earth. Astronauts can record measurements and review their status, while CMOs and flight surgeons can review alerts and verify follow-up tasks.

The system was built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, FastAPI, Python, SQLite, WebSockets, pandas, PyArrow, and Recharts.

We built this app with the assumption that NASA missions have integrated the same technology in which the databases were built, meaning that websockets can be used to measure second to second if the project is approved, rigth now the demo has a .json form the databases that "simulates" with real data the fligth process. Obviously the rest of the data that involves fluids, such as blood and urine are complements (also based on real databases) that are used for tracking in long term. On the other hand, radiation/muscle loss are add ons that were completeley simulated due to the time available for building this demo.
